subject: Q3 GPU pool allocation - exception request & cross-team asks
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, Emma Lin <emma@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: procure@acmeprocure.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 GPU pool allocation - exception request & cross-team asks

Team — looping everyone in so we can decide on a short-term exception for Nimbus's Q3 trial. Short summary: Nimbus is proposing a 6-week high-throughput proof-of-value starting 2026-07-05. They want a dedicated pool commitment during the first three weeks to guarantee latency at scale, then autoscale down afterwards. Sales has signaled this is a high-visibility account (DEAL-7892) and Finance is willing to consider a one-off reservation if Product/Infra confirm capacity and constraints.

Key asks for the thread:
- Product (jonas): can we support a temporary minimum pool with capped burst (3 weeks)? What are risk/rollback options?
- Infra/Eng (laura): what does this mean operationally for Q3 pool allocations? Can you reserve N GPUs and tune autoscaling policies for a temporary exception?
- Solutions (dev): what config will we hand to Nimbus (min_instances, burst_policy, prewarm)?
- Procurement (procure@acmeprocure.com): can you provision a short-term reservation contract and surface billing implications?

I attached a draft Q3 plan and a cost estimate for the proposed reservation (q3-dedicated-plan-v2.xlsx, pool-cost-estimate.csv). Emma — appreciate any constraints from Nimbus (SLA, expected qps) so we can size.

Proposed timeline:
- Decision by 2026-06-03 so engineering can schedule capacity changes
- Reservation in place by 2026-06-23 for a 07/05 start

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Emma Lin <emma@nimbus-analytics.com>, procure@acmeprocure.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 GPU pool allocation - exception request & cross-team asks

Thanks, Evelyn — good summary. High-level response from infra: we can support a temporary reservation but need clear guardrails. A few immediate questions before I can commit numbers: 

1) Target min capacity: is this an exact GPU count or percent of their observed peak?
2) Burst behavior: do we allow unlimited burst up to node capacity, or cap at X concurrent requests?
3) Rollback/fallback: if other customers hit capacity, what's the priority? Can we route to a lower-cost model variant instead of throttling?

Operational implications: reserving a contiguous GPU pool for three weeks will reduce available autoscaling headroom in the US-west region by the same amount. If we commit now, we'll need to:
- update the autoscaler policy to pin min_instances for the pool
- implement burst caps and request-weighting so Nimbus can't starve shared queues
- schedule prewarm “cold start” windows the week before start date

I'll need numbers (GPU count, expected concurrency, target 95th latency) to produce a cost + risk statement. If anyone can supply those, I’ll run a quick simulation.

- Laura
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Emma Lin <emma@nimbus-analytics.com>, procure@acmeprocure.com
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 GPU pool allocation - exception request & cross-team asks

Adding ops/solutions perspective. Based on Nimbus's trial brief (Emma, thanks for the numbers shared privately): expected sustained 120 rps with 8k token avg context, peak spikes to ~220 rps. My recommended short-term config: 

- reserve: 20x A100-equivalent GPUs (estimate to achieve 95th latency under sustained load)
- min_instances: set to 20 for the dedicated pool during 07/05 - 07/26
- burst_policy: allow 40% burst above min but cap request concurrency per session to 10
- prewarm: 24h rolling prewarm prior to start (reduce tail latency)

Operational notes / tradeoffs:
- Cost: see attached CSV estimate. This reservation increases P99 cost by ~48% for that pool week but keeps tail latency within SLA.
- Fallback: implement automatic downgrade to a smaller quantized model variant (q2-small-8bit) if overall cluster utilization across the region exceeds 85%. That avoids global throttling but may affect output quality.

If Finance signs off on the one-off reservation fee and Product confirms the capped burst approach, Infra can implement the policy changes two weeks out.

Config snippet (for infra automation):

min_instances: 20
burst_above_min_pct: 40
burst_concurrency_cap_per_session: 10
fallback_model: q2-small-8bit
prewarm_window_hours: 24

- Dev
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

All — thanks for the quick input. From Product's side: I'm comfortable approving a one-off exception under these constraints, provided Finance signs off on the reservation terms and we commit to the fallback model path. A couple of clarifications I need before final approval: 

- SLA target: confirm 95th latency target (Evelyn/Emma) and whether trial requires hard SLA or just guideline for the PoV.
- Metrics & telemetry: Infra must expose a short dashboard (tokens/sec, 95/99 latency, cluster utilization) to both Nimbus and our team during the trial window.
- Communication plan: we need a one-page runbook for on-call (who owns incident escalation during the trial?).

If Finance confirms the fee, I'll mark this as an approved product exception and we can schedule the rollout.

-Jonas
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — here is the decision pathway and immediate next steps. Summary of agreed points: 

- We will provision a 3-week minimum reservation: 20 GPUs (A100-equivalent) for 07/05–07/26 with the burst_policy and fallback model Dev outlined.
- Product (Jonas) is approving the exception contingent on Finance signoff for the reservation fee.
- Infra (Laura) will prepare the autoscale changes and the telemetry dashboard.
- Solutions (Dev) will produce the final config and run the prewarm plan.
- Procurement (procure@acmeprocure.com) — please prepare a short-term reservation contract (one-off) and return with the fee and billing schedule by EOD 2026-06-03.

Emma — can you confirm the 95th latency target you require (or confirm "guideline") and sign the runbook once we share it?

I attached the updated Q3 plan with the Nimbus slot highlighted (q3-dedicated-plan-v2.xlsx) and the updated cost CSV (pool-cost-estimate.csv). Also adding the HubSpot link for DEAL-7892 and the DocSend link to the PoV brief above.

If procurement returns a fee that looks reasonable, Jonas will finalize the product exception and Infra will schedule the capacity changes in the 2026-06-10 maintenance window.

I'll follow up with a brief doc and a one-page runbook draft by 2026-06-02.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Operations
